# Home-Field Advantage

> **Two source classes on this page, never mixed in one claim.** *How the guide defines it*, *how the guide uses it* and every page reference are **GUIDE CONTENT**. *Working definition*, *why it matters* and any arithmetic over printed figures are **TTW DERIVED** — this library's words, supplied because the guide supplies none. Where the guide neither defines nor develops a concept, the field reads `Not addressed in guide.` and is not padded out.

> Appears on **143 pages** of 345. A high count usually means the concept is woven through the 138 team tables, not that the guide discusses it that often — this is a count of locations, not of emphasis.

## How the guide defines it

p. 2 glosses `HOME FA – Home Field Advantage` and `ROAD FA – Road Field Advantage`.

## How the guide uses it

p. 21 is a standalone feature, 'Quantifying College Football's Biggest Advantage'. Its stated position is that home-field advantage is more dynamic than ever and that one simple baseline is probably not enough, but that having something is better than nothing. Every team then carries its own home and road field rating in the conference tables, and those two numbers are what turn a rating difference into a projected line.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

A per-team points adjustment applied to a power rating, expressed separately for home and road, rather than a single league-wide constant.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the difference between a rating and a line. The guide's decision to give every team its own home and road figure — rather than adding a flat three points — is what lets the same rating produce different lines in different stadiums.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Mechanically. Phase 6 established that the printed line is the home team's rating plus its home field rating, minus the away team's rating plus its road field rating. At neutral sites Makinen puts both teams on their road ratings.

## Where it appears

p. 21 for the reasoning; p. 46 for the ratings; every conference table for the per-team home and road figures.
